Authored the M0 mamba body-rewire (the GPU-iteration-gated integration of the dormant scaffold) under #if SG_TUNED_MB_PROJ_WGMMA, split cleanly into two independently-gated sub-levers, in my isolated worktree only.

FWD-GEMM HALF (transport-only by construction, gate-green-by-precedent, CPU-provable non-perturbing):
- C1 in P0: mb_proj_wbf_convert fills the bf16 projection-weight cache (fenced by B0).
- New mbtc_materialize_sample_x (in model_stage_mamba_tc.cuh) called in P1 after each sample's mb_forward_sample (before mb_backward_sample reuses smem / before the next sample overwrites it): materializes the 5 converted projections' INPUTS X (in/out/gate/up/down) to the MbActs HBM region at rows [b*kSeq, b*kSeq+kSeq). xn and h1n (not retained by the scalar fwd) are recomputed with the IDENTICAL fp32 RMSNorm the oracle ran (same multiply association); y_gated and prod from retained LayerAct. Every stored value is __float2bfloat16 of the exact oracle fp32 -> bf16-rounded reference, element-owned, no reduction/atomics. The scan + scalar fwd/bwd are byte-for-byte untouched, and nothing consumes these acts until the dW half goes LIVE, so turning the fwd half ON changes grads NOT AT ALL (only adds plumbing) -- verifiably transport-only.

dW HALF (needs-parity-fp32-reassoc, S1-class, GPU-only-revalidatable) -- structured + compiled but the parity-bearing step reported as TODO:
- A P2-dW output-stationary phase (mbtc_proj_dw_run_tile, gt % nCTA ownership, full-T K-contraction, ascending-t, no atomics) that overwrites the 5 weights' reduced grad with the reassociated wgmma dW. Gated under SG_TUNED_MB_PROJ_WGMMA_DW (defaults to the master; set =0 to land the fwd half alone -- the decoder fold-A-reverts-alone discipline).
- The dY-adjoint capture (dY_in=[dx_main|dz], dY_outp, dY_gate, dY_up, dY_down) is TRANSIENT in the scalar bwd, so capturing it needs hooks inside mb_backward_sample/mb_mixer_bwd/mb_swiglu_bwd. That is the parity-changing, GPU-only step and is LEFT AS THE EXPLICIT TODO. The actual grad overwrite is double-guarded by SG_TUNED_MB_PROJ_WGMMA_DW_LIVE (default OFF) so the GEMM machinery compiles/reviews without risking zeroed grads before dY is wired.

authored.fix:
THREE fixes authored, CPU-verified, zero single-GPU risk (test-only scaffolding):

DP-1 (tests/hw/test_dp2_loopback_determinism.py):
The near-tautological assert (a) was replaced with a PRE-GATHER cross-rank owned-shard-vs-reference parity check. The old assert compared post-gather full params from both ranks which are byte-identical BY CONSTRUCTION (built from all_gather_into_tensor), making it a no-op detector for per-rank apply bugs. The fix: _run_decomposed_step now returns (full, loss, Bw, owned_shard_clone, s, e) where owned_shard_clone is cloned BEFORE step [4] all-gather. In worker_main, each rank's pre-gather owned shard is all-gathered into a per=ceil(total/world) padded buffer; every rank then checks that all ranks' owned shards match the same-positioned slices of the single-GPU reference (ref, already computed for assert (c)) within _PARITY_TOL. A per-rank apply bug (wrong slice math, wrong state-plane offset, asymmetric scalar) diverges HERE — the gather no longer launders it. Existing (b) A/A/A bit-exact and (c) fp64-anchored parity-vs-single-GPU are preserved unchanged.

DP-2 (tests/hw/test_3d_parallel.py):
test_3d_parallel_smoke previously asserted only thr > 0.0. Three invariants added:
(1) Deterministic same-seed param init: _build_local_shard gains a seed parameter (default 42) and calls torch.manual_seed(seed+idx) before each torch.randn — every DP rank starts from byte-identical weights, which is the precondition for the cross-DP param-identity assert (independent randn per rank would make post-step params legitimately differ across DP replicas even when ZeRO-3 is correct).
(2) ZeRO3Sharder shard-coverage assert (single-process safe): after partition_optimizer_state, each param's shard_info is checked: 0 <= start <= end <= numel, and numel == p.numel(). This verifies the live sharder._shards are sane (mirrors test_zero3_partition_covers_param_exactly on the live object).
(3) Cross-DP param-identity invariant (fires only when DP>1 and torch.distributed initialized): after the steps loop, for each named param, all_gather_into_tensor the full param across the DP group (after all_gather_params every DP rank already holds the full param) and assert torch.equal(rank_0_slice, rank_r_slice) for r in 1..dp. A sharding/collective regression in ZeRO-3 reduce-scatter or all-gather will fail this assert even if throughput is positive.

ZeRO-3 broadcast path (grokking_optimizers/parallel/zero3.py gather_full, lines 236-242):
Verified CORRECT — no change. The tensor-granular broadcast path calls dist.broadcast(full[s:e], src=r, group=group) for all r. The seg = full[s:e] slices are contiguous 1D views of a contiguous full tensor (confirmed in code and with a live Python test). The prior workflow correctly rejected the "non-contiguous broadcast" premise. The logic is also correct for the source rank: when r == self.rank, seg already has the correct data from the owned() loop, and the broadcast is still called (correctly — broadcast is collective, the source rank must enter it). No bug, no change.

tp_transport.cuh LoopbackTransport verified: peer() is pure pointer arithmetic (no nvshmem_ptr call) — LoopbackTransport is A/A/A-safe. The nvshmem_ptr-per-element register pressure concern (P2-5) is specific to NvshmemTransport (compiled only under -DSG_HAS_NVSHMEM=1), not LoopbackTransport.

authored.notes: ZeRO-3 broadcast path: VERIFIED CORRECT, NO CHANGE. The prior workflow correctly rejected the false "non-contiguous broadcast" premise. Slices from flat_plan_for_optimizer are always contiguous 1D views of a contiguous full tensor (full = torch.empty(plan.total, ...); full[s:e] is always contiguous for a 1D tensor). The source-rank-pass pattern (if r == self.rank: pass; then dist.broadcast(...)) is correct: the pass says no extra copy is needed (shard already in full from owned() loop), and broadcast is still called because it is a collective requiring all ranks to enter. LoopbackTransport in tp_transport.cuh is A/A/A-safe: peer() is heap_base + pe*stride + off (pure pointer arithmetic), NOT nvshmem_ptr; the ascending-pe fixed-order accumulation in tp_allreduce_sum_fixed_order is structural determinism. The nvshmem_ptr-per-element register pressure risk (P2-5) is isolated to NvshmemTransport (guarded by #if defined(SG_HAS_NVSHMEM)) and irrelevant to LoopbackTransport.
